content:
Facts: Grandchildren of the deceased, called by representation, brought an action for reduction alleging infringement of their legitimate share, after having received sums of money pursuant to a testamentary legacy expressly granted in lieu of the legitimate portion. Several years after receipt, they declared their intention to renounce the legacy and to claim their reserved share.
Legal framework
Articles 551, 649, 653, 536 ff. ICC on legacy in lieu of the legitimate share, acquisition and renunciation of legacies, and protection of forced heirs; principles on tacit acceptance and renunciation of testamentary benefits; settled Supreme Court case law on the irrevocability of the choice between substitute legacy and legitimate share.
Interpretative issue
Whether a beneficiary who has received and retained a legacy expressly granted in lieu of the legitimate portion may subsequently renounce it and validly bring an action for reduction, and what conduct constitutes an unequivocal manifestation of the will to retain the substitute legacy.
Principle applied
A legacy expressly granted in lieu of the legitimate share under Article 551 ICC is acquired automatically, subject to the beneficiary’s right to renounce it. However, once the beneficiary has received and retained the legacy, thereby manifesting—expressly or tacitly—the intention to keep it, the right to choose between the substitute legacy and the claim to the legitimate portion is definitively lost ope legis. Generic reservations or subsequent declarations of renunciation, especially if unaccompanied by restitution of the sums received, are ineffective and cannot revive the forfeited right to seek reduction.
